title: Minority Soldiers Leave the Ranks
narrative: The declaration of a Bosniak national state lands in the barracks. Serb and Croat soldiers who had served the Republic find the foundations shifting beneath them. A slow trickle becomes a quiet exodus — not a mutiny, but a thousand personal decisions to go home, cross the line, or simply disappear from the rolls. Recruitment officers report a noticeable cooling in the multi-ethnic towns.

effect.text: Minority soldiers quietly leave the ARBiH ranks.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 6. Reflects real 1992 ARBiH debates documented in Ramet, 'Thinking about Yugoslavia' (2005), and Burg & Shoup, 'The War in Bosnia-Herzegovina' (2000).

title: A Nation Under Siege
narrative: The identity decision hardens into resolve. By late 1993 the civic republican rhetoric has faded; the mosque, the neighborhood, and the language carry the appeal to arms. Mobilization offices see longer queues and shorter discussions. What has been lost in international legitimacy is recovered, at least for now, in the willingness of the survivors to fight.

effect.text: Bosniak ethnic solidarity powers ARBiH recruitment.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 6. Reflects the real radicalization curve inside ARBiH through 1993 documented in Hoare, 'How Bosnia Armed' (2004).

title: The World Stops Listening
narrative: Foreign mediators who once championed Sarajevo as the last multi-ethnic capital now brief their governments in a different tone. The platform has not been revoked, but the briefings about ethnic institutions and exclusive recruitment have gone back to capitals that care. The Contact Group begins preparing for a Bosnia that looks like a Bosniak entity, not a republic — and negotiates accordingly.

effect.text: International mediators treat RBiH as ethnic party, not civic state.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 6. Counterfactual mirror of Contact Group diplomatic calculus 1993-94.

title: The Pocket Falls
narrative: The 5th Corps has held against VRS, RSK, and Abdic's APWB for almost two years. The arithmetic of siege outlasts the arithmetic of defenders: no airdrops, no reinforcement road, no column of volunteers left to march in. The RBiH defensive perimeter breaks in sectors and does not close again. Refugees cross into Croatian territory by the tens of thousands. A Corps that had been a national symbol becomes a casualty list.

effect.text: The Bihac pocket collapses. 5th Corps is destroyed or captured.

historical_source: Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 4. Counterfactual to the historical 5th Corps breakout of 1995.

title: Northwest Front Freed
narrative: With Bihac eliminated as an open wound, the VRS 2nd Krajina Corps redeploys. Fifteen to twenty brigades that had been tied down for two years walk out of the Bihac perimeter and onto trucks for central Bosnia. The strategic picture shifts faster than any single operation could ever shift it. The RS political leadership smells the end of the war — on its terms.

effect.text: VRS 2nd Krajina Corps redeploys to central Bosnia.

title: A Quarter Million on the Move
narrative: The displaced of Bihac do not stop at the first line of safety. Croatia's temporary camps overflow within weeks; the columns reach the Neretva, the Lasva, the Bosna. ARBiH supply officers compete with UNHCR for the same trucks, the same fuel, the same calories. International coverage hardens — but the people are already cold, and damage to the RBiH manpower system is already done.

effect.text: A massive refugee wave floods RBiH-held central Bosnia.

title: The Camps Are Found
narrative: Foreign journalists and ICRC delegations reach the network of detention facilities across the Prijedor and Banja Luka regions ahead of the historical ITN broadcast of 6 August 1992. With RS political leadership committed to maximum force, the chain of command around Omarska, Keraterm, and Trnopolje is less disciplined and less concealed than in the historical record. Photographs reach London, Paris, and Washington earlier; capitals that had been preparing slow responses find themselves answering morning cables. Belgrade notes, privately, that the arithmetic of plausible deniability has shifted against it.

effect.text: Detention-camp documentation reaches Western capitals weeks earlier than in the historical record.

historical_source: ICTY Stakic Trial Judgment (IT-97-24-T) and Kvocka et al. Trial Judgment (IT-98-30/1-T) on Omarska, Keraterm, and Trnopolje detention facilities; Tadic Trial Judgment (IT-94-1-T) on camp structure. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: ICTY Opens Its Doors Early
narrative: The accumulating record of atrocities reaches a political threshold the Security Council cannot defer. The International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia is stood up with expanded indictment authority; early subpoenas reach Pale and Belgrade. Serbian President Milosevic, calculating costs, orders a quiet pullback of logistical and personnel channels that had connected the VJ to the VRS. Karadzic and Mladic learn the shape of their defense through their lawyers, not through public argument.

effect.text: ICTY mandate expanded; Belgrade distances itself from the VRS earlier than in history.

historical_source: UNSCR 827 (25 May 1993) established the ICTY. Counterfactual: earlier and more heavily-resourced mandate in response to accumulated aggressive-goals evidence. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: Safe Areas With Teeth
narrative: UNSCR 819, 824, and 836 arrive in the counterfactual with the mandate and the rules of engagement the historical resolutions lacked. Dutch and French detachments arrive at Srebrenica, Gorazde, Zepa, and Bihac with artillery and close-air-support tasking, not only with logistic and observer roles. VRS corps commanders in Drinski and eastern axes receive written guidance that operations against those perimeters will be met with NATO response. The arithmetic of the enclaves changes: they cease to be siege objectives and begin to be diplomatic preconditions.

effect.text: UN Safe Areas arrive with a defence mandate; RS operations against Bihac, Srebrenica, Gorazde, and Zepa are constrained.

historical_source: UNSCR 819 (16 April 1993) — Srebrenica safe area; UNSCR 824 (6 May 1993) — six safe areas; UNSCR 836 (4 June 1993) — defence mandate. ICTY Krstic Trial Judgment (IT-98-33-T) documented that the historical mandate fell short; this counterfactual models the enforced version. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.

title: NATO Will Not Wait for Markale
narrative: Cumulative ICTY evidence and the documented shelling of civilian infrastructure drag the NATO threshold forward by more than a year. Allied Force commanders receive strike authorisations that in the historical record waited until August 1995. The VRS loses the freedom of movement it had relied on through 1994; front-line commanders begin to plan their operations around coverage windows of the no-fly zone rather than around the enemy. The war's endgame window has closed on Republika Srpska earlier than Mladic's staff had projected.

effect.text: NATO intervention threshold lowered; VRS operational freedom constrained.

historical_source: Operation Deliberate Force (30 August - 20 September 1995) was the historical turning point; counterfactual moves that threshold earlier in response to cumulative aggressive-goals evidence. Plan: docs/plans/2026-03-24-v090-consequence-system-plan.md Chain 5.
